title: Thinking Deeper in Gemini — Jack Rae, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Jack Rae explains Gemini's 'thinking' as dynamic test-time compute: a model emits intermediate reasoning tokens in a loop, trained via RL with sparse correct/incorrect rewards, letting it self-correct, decompose problems, and explore parallel chains. He frames progress as removing bottlenecks and pitches thinking budgets as a continuous cost/quality slider plus 'deep think' high-budget async modes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of picking a discrete model size, they expose a continuous thinking-token budget so cheap tasks get little compute and hard tasks get more, chosen per task class.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Now with thinking we can have a continuous uh budget uh which allows you to have a much more granular slider of how much capability you want

takeaways.technique: Route by difficulty, not just price
takeaways.what_they_do: Model learns to apply less compute to simple requests and more to hard ones, dynamically, rather than a fixed amount per call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: less compute for simpler requests, more compute for harder requests and have this process be very dynamic

takeaways.what_they_do: RL-trained thinking traces show the model posing a hypothesis, testing it, rejecting it, and trying alternatives before committing to an answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it rejects its own idea and then it tries an alternative approach

takeaways.technique: Parallel chains of thought that integrate
takeaways.what_they_do: Deep Think runs multiple parallel reasoning chains and merges them into one stronger answer for very hard problems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we leverage much deeper chains of thought uh and parallel uh chains of thought that can integrate with each other
takeaways.numbers: USAMO: 2.5 Pro ~50th percentile, Deep Think ~65th percentile

takeaways.what_they_do: Deep Research/Deep Think accept a hard query, run asynchronously for a long time, and return a stronger result later.
takeaways.evidence_quote: fire off the query and then have some asynchronous process that's running for a while and you'll come back

takeaways.what_they_do: Training uses only a vague correct/incorrect signal and still shapes useful reasoning behavior, implying outcome-only feedback is enough to improve strategy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model is able to just get a very vague signal of what is correct, what is not correct
